When deciding how to split a rating scale into "positive" and "negative," the main factor I considered was the real-world consequence of a mediocre score. For a doctor, a 3-out-of-5 rating is often a serious red flag, because patients expect and demand consistently high-quality care. In that context, a 3 usually implies long waits, poor communication, or misdiagnosis risk, so I would classify 1–3 as negative and only 4–5 as truly positive. For a restaurant, however, a 3 is far more neutral or even slightly favorable, since dining is subjective and people often reserve 5s for exceptional experiences. There, I might classify 1–2 as negative, 3 as neutral, and 4–5 as positive.
